newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Feb 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Feb 14.

text.p: Serious Fraud Office director Chas Sturt was seen by his staff as not competent to investigate the Winebox documents, the Cook Islands tax commission of inquiry was told on Thursday. Former Serious Fraud Office senior prosecutor Susan Pilgrim, a lawyer who ended a six-year career with the office in September, described a Monday meeting at which Sturt spoke of rumours that staff were concerned that no lawyer had been assigned to the Winebox investigation. "I recall he was very angry at this suggestion and reminded the staff that he was the lawyer on the Winebox investigation." Page 1.

Australia's national archives have been asked by the New Zealand government not to reveal previously classified documents without notifying officials. The request came after embarrassment earlier this year when documents were made public saying Australia secretly lent A$20 million to bail New Zealand out of a balance-of-payments crisis 30 years ago. Page 2.

The police will be asked by Labour police spokesman George Hawkins to detail how many officers have faced criminal charges in the past five years. Hawkins will also seek a breakdown on the type of charges when he puts written question to Police Minister Jack Elder next week. Page 2.

Maori broadcasting funding agency Te Mangai Paho did not deliberately withhold information from the government about inadequate financial controls at Aotearoa Television Network, chief executive Mike Hollings said on Thursday. He said Te Mangai Paho had not completed a management audit of ATN when the government began considering last month whether to provide further funding for the pilot television station. Page 2.

Corporate dairy farmer Tasman Agriculture's half-year profit slumped 87 percent to NZ$210,000, despite increased milk production and a 19 percent boost in sales revenue. The company has suspended its dividend after announcing that tax-paid profit for the six months to November fell to $210,000 compared to the 1995 period's $1.58 million. Page 14.

Struggling exporters face yet another climb in the dollar from the middle of this year, after a short breather as the currency eases off till June, according to Bankers Trust. The dollar was 68.66 on the trade-weighted index on Thursday, and was expected to fall temporarily in the middle of the year before rising to 70 on the index by mid-1998, says Bankers Trust. In a report on the exchange rate, BT says the dollar should weaken further as the Reserve Bank maintains an easing bias in monetary conditions. Page 14.

Television New Zealand wants to lift its stake in pay TV operator Sky Network Television in what chief executive Chris Anderson has described as a joint venture with global media giant News Corporation. News Corporation's subsidiary, Wellington-based Independent Newspapers, has been negotiating to buy a majority stake in Sky since October. Page 14.

Listed eftpos technology company Advantage Group reported on Thursday a $1.29 million bottom-line profit in the six months to December, down 2.57 percent on last year. The profit was on total operating revenue of $26.88 million from $26.22 million last year. Slightly less than half the revenue came from Australia. Page 14.

Christchurch-based Dairy Brands forecast it would post a $900,000 profit in the eight months to May, excluding any one-off items. This would be an improvement on the $249,000 profit the company reported in the 12 months to September 30 in its first full year as a public listed company. Page 14.

Cinema operator Force Corporation reported on Thursday a 68 percent improvement in bottom-line profit for the six months to December 31. The net profit of $2.60 million was up from $1.54 million in the corresponding period of 1995, with revenue up 11.8 percent from $11.96 million to $13.38 million. Pre-tax earnings of $3.79 million were up from $2.65 million. Page 14.

A depressed local carpet market and the strong currency put Cavalier Corporation's after-tax profit down 17.4 percent in the half-year to December 31. The company said full-year results were unlikely to match 1995-96. Cavalier told the Stock Exchange that operating revenue for the six months to December was $96.7 million, 8.6 percent down on the December 1995 half-year. Page 14.
